title: Indian Mall Worker Stabbed 15 Times in Utah After Attacker Asked 'Are You Muslim?'
excerpt: Syed Sohail Uddin remains in critical condition after a hate-motivated attack at Valley Fair Mall. The suspect told police he 'intends to kill Muslims.'
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Syed Sohail Uddin was stabbed 15 times in a hate-motivated attack in Utah.
  • Suspect Peter Michael Larsen expressed intent to kill Muslims and planned mass casualty events.
  • Bystanders intervened, disarming the attacker before police arrived; Uddin is in critical condition.
  • The Indian Consulate is coordinating with local authorities and supporting Uddin's family.
  • The incident highlights rising anti-Muslim violence and safety concerns for the Indian diaspora.

Uddin's Status
Police reports and eyewitness accounts
  • Syed Sohail Uddin, an Indian-origin kiosk worker from Hyderabad, was stabbed 15 times at Valley Fair Mall in West Valley City, Utah
  • Suspect Peter Michael Larsen, 48, told police he "intends to kill Muslims" and had planned mass casualty events
  • Bystanders tackled and disarmed the attacker before police arrived; Uddin remains in critical condition requiring multiple surgeries
  • The Indian Consulate in San Francisco has reached out to the victim's family and is coordinating with local authorities

An Indian-origin mall worker is fighting for his life in a Utah hospital after being stabbed 15 times in what authorities describe as a religiously motivated attack at a shopping mall in West Valley City.

Syed Sohail Uddin, who worked at a kiosk inside Valley Fair Mall, sustained life-threatening injuries to his hands, heart and lungs during Monday's assault, according to police documents and local Muslim community leaders. He has undergone multiple surgeries and remains in critical condition.

The Attack

According to a police booking affidavit and accounts from Imam Shuaib Din of the Utah Islamic Center, the suspect, 48-year-old Peter Michael Larsen, approached Uddin's kiosk and asked for his name, inquired whether he was Muslim, and then requested a bottle of water. When Uddin turned to retrieve the bottle, Larsen drew a knife and began stabbing him repeatedly.

Police received multiple 911 calls around 2:30 p.m. local time reporting two men "involved in a physical altercation where one male was stabbing the other," according to the affidavit filed in court. When officers arrived, bystanders had already pinned Larsen to the ground and removed the knife from his hand.

"He had targeted the victim with intent to kill him because of his religion."

— Police booking affidavit, West Valley City

The victim was "bleeding profusely" and was rushed to the hospital, according to Reuters. Larsen was also hospitalized for injuries sustained while being subdued by bystanders before being booked into Salt Lake County Jail.

Suspect's Statements Reveal Premeditated Intent

Court documents reveal chilling details about Larsen's motives. Police said Larsen told investigators he "intends to kill Muslims" and that he posed "a substantial danger to the public if released based on his violent actions today, ideologies and pre-planned mass casualty events."

A coworker, Luna Nunez, who later visited Uddin in the hospital, told The New York Times that Larsen had asked the victim "where he was from, his name and if he was Muslim" before launching the assault. A GoFundMe campaign organized by friends identified the victim and stated he was stabbed 15 times and required multiple surgeries.

Indian Consulate Responds

The Consulate General of India in San Francisco issued a statement expressing grief over the incident. "The Consulate is in close contact with the friends and family and stands ready to provide all possible consular assistance," the statement said. "We remain engaged with local authorities and will continue to monitor the matter closely."

Rising Anti-Muslim Violence in the US

The attack has drawn comparisons to other recent incidents of anti-Muslim violence in the United States, including a May shooting at an Islamic center in San Diego by two teenagers that killed three people. The Council on American-Islamic Relations condemned the Utah assault, calling it "yet another reminder that anti-Muslim rhetoric has real-world consequences."

Civil rights groups have warned that inflammatory rhetoric against Muslims can fuel real-world attacks, particularly in the current political climate. For the Indian diaspora community, the incident underscores growing safety concerns, as Indian-origin individuals have been increasingly targeted in hate crimes across the country.

Larsen remains in custody at Salt Lake County Jail. Formal charges have not yet been announced, though the investigation is ongoing and the police affidavit references attempted murder.
